entries.text: A hard-working farmer ought to be the first to partake of his crops.

text.text: The husbandman that laboureth must be first partaker of the fruits.

entries.text: He that sows sparingly shall also reap sparingly; and he which sows bountifully shall also reap bountifully.

text.text: But this I say, He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully.

entries.text: The sluggard will not plow by reason of the cold; therefore shall he beg in harvest, and have nothing.

text.text: The sluggard will not plow by reason of the cold; therefore shall he beg in harvest, and have nothing.

entries.text: He that tills his land shall have plenty of bread; but he that follows after vain persons shall have poverty.

text.text: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread: but he that followeth after vain persons shall have poverty enough.

entries.text: You shall eat the labor of your hands, and it shall be well with you.

text.text: For thou shalt eat the labour of thine hands: happy shalt thou be, and it shall be well with thee.

entries.text: The fields of the slothful will be overgrown with thistles and weeds, his farm broken down, and he will fall into poverty.

text.text: I went by the field of the slothful, and by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;
And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, and nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down.
Then I saw, and considered it well: I looked upon it, and received instruction.
Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:
So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth; and thy want as an armed man.

entries.text: Be not overly concerned about the weather when you sow and reap, for you do not know the works of God.

text.text: He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.
As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child: even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.
In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.
